feedback.problem:
A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration $a(t)={e}^{3t},$ where $t\ge 0$ is the time. If the particle has position $x=0$ and velocity $v=1$ when $t=0,$ the position $x$ of the particle at time $t$ is

$x(t)=$
{{field-1}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
We start by integrating the acceleration to get the velocity $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int {e}^{3t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{e}^{3t}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C,$ we use the fact that $v(0)=1.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =\frac{1}{3}{e}^{0}+C \\ 1 & =\frac{1}{3}+C \\ C & =\frac{2}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

So the velocity is given by $v(t)=\frac{1}{3}{e}^{3t}+\frac{2}{3}.$

Now, we integrate the velocity to get $x(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =\int v(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int (\frac{1}{3}{e}^{3t}+\frac{2}{3})\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\int {e}^{3t}\,\text{d}t+\frac{2}{3}\int \,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{1}{9}{e}^{3t}+\frac{2}{3}t+K\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $K$, we use the fact that $x(0)=0.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}0 & =\frac{1}{9}{e}^{0}+\frac{2}{3}(0)+K \\ 0 & =\frac{1}{9}+K \\ K & =-\frac{1}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the position $x$ of the particle at time $t$ is 

$$
x(t)=\frac{1}{9}{e}^{3t}+\frac{2}{3}t-\frac{1}{9}.
$$
